snippets.headline: Average latest A1c summarizes recorded A1c values and is separate from testing compliance and control rates.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The average latest A1c percentage among tested patients is represented by `AVG(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value)`. In clinic-level GSD reporting, this appears alongside `COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS good_control_rate`, and `COUNT_IF(a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS poor_control_rate`. The numerator for the average is the A1c evidence value, and the intended denominator is the count of rows with non-null `evidence_value` included by `AVG`. Use this only for A1c-tested evidence analysis; it is not a compliance rate.

snippets.headline: Clinic-level Glycemic Status reporting combines eligible counts, testing compliance, control rates, and average latest A1c.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For clinic-level GSD reporting, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` directly because `clinic_id` is present on the GSD patient-level table. The curated clinic query groups by `clinic_id` and computes `COUNT(*) AS eligible_patients`, `COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS good_control_rate`, `COUNT_IF(a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(numerator_flag) AS poor_control_rate`, and `AVG(evidence_value) AS avg_latest_a1c`. Here the GSD compliance denominator is all eligible patients in that clinic, while good and poor control denominators are only patients with `numerator_flag`. This pattern is the source for clinic-level A1c testing and control comparison.

snippets.headline: Glycemic control rates measure results among tested patients, while Glycemic Status compliance measures testing among all eligible patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For GSD, good and poor glycemic control rates are computed only among A1c-tested patients, not all eligible diabetic patients. The good control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, where the denominator is the count of tested patients. The poor control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, using the same tested-patient denominator. This differs from GSD compliance rate, whose denominator is all eligible GSD patients: `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`.

snippets.headline: Glycemic control bands combine A1c testing status with good, moderate, and poor result categories.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Use the derived GSD glycemic control band expression to classify A1c testing and control outcomes. The exact expression is `CASE WHEN NOT gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag THEN 'Not tested' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_lt8 THEN 'Good (<8%)' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_gt9 THEN 'Poor (>9%)' ELSE 'Moderate (8-9%)' END`. The complete output value list is `Not tested`, `Good (<8%)`, `Poor (>9%)`, and `Moderate (8-9%)`. This band combines the testing status and A1c result category, so `Not tested` is a testing gap rather than a clinical control range.

snippets.headline: Glycemic Status Assessment measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had an A1c test during the year.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets GSD when they have an A1c test in the measurement year, represented in patient detail by `gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag`. The standard patient-level compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all eligible rows in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` at the grouping grain. For the governed overall rate, query `SELECT MEASURE(`GSD Compliance Rate`) AS gsd_compliance_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gsd_compliance_metrics`.

snippets.headline: GSD measures whether diabetic adults aged 18 through 75 received an A1c test during the measurement year.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment. Its eligible population is diabetic patients aged 18-75, and compliance requires an A1c test in the measurement year. Retrieve the rate with `SELECT MEASURE(`GSD Compliance Rate`) AS gsd_compliance_rate FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gsd_compliance_metrics`. For patient-level evidence or care gaps, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` instead of the metric view.

snippets.headline: Eye Exam patients use Glycemic Status rows for clinic and panel attribution when reporting clinic-level rates.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Attach clinic or panel attribution to EED patients by joining `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_eed` to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` on `gold_adherence_eed.patient_id = gold_adherence_gsd.patient_id AND gold_adherence_eed.measurement_year = gold_adherence_gsd.measurement_year`. The curated relationship is many-to-one from EED to GSD, and every EED patient has a GSD row. Use this join to bring `clinic_id` and `panel_id` onto EED rows for clinic or panel breakdowns. A verified sample computes clinic EED rate as `COUNT_IF(e.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)` after this join and groups by `g.clinic_id`.

snippets.headline: Clinic-level comparisons across diabetes measures use Glycemic Status attribution and report each measure’s eligible clinic-attributed patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For clinic-level comparisons across all five diabetes measures, the curated pattern uses GSD as the clinic attribution source. The union labels the complete measure set as `GSD`, `KED`, `BPD`, `SPD`, and `EED`, each carrying `measurement_year`, `clinic_id`, and `numerator_flag`; KED, BPD, SPD, and EED are joined to the GSD clinic CTE by `patient_id` and `measurement_year`. The clinic rates are `COUNT_IF(measure = '<MEASURE>' AND numerator_flag) / COUNT_IF(measure = '<MEASURE>')` for each measure. Because the KED branch uses an inner join to GSD, clinic-level KED rates represent clinic-attributed KED patients rather than all KED-eligible patients aged 18-85.

snippets.headline: GSD gaps represent missing annual A1c testing, while KED gaps distinguish missing kidney tests using both eGFR and uACR flags.
snippets.source: Query history for eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked
snippets.content: For rows included with `status = 'NOT_MET'`, GSD is labeled `'No A1c test in year'`. KED uses the complete conditional classification: when `NOT egfr_flag AND NOT uacr_flag`, the reason is `'No eGFR and no uACR'`; when `NOT uacr_flag` otherwise, it is `'No uACR test'`; otherwise, it is `'No eGFR test'`. These labels are produced from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` and `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked`, and the resulting rows are counted with `COUNT(*)` by measure and gap reason. The KED labels are mutually assigned by CASE order, so the first label applies when both tests are absent.

snippets.headline: Kidney Evaluation outreach for closing uACR gaps targets patients who already completed eGFR but lack uACR.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: KED care gap outreach has a specific filter for patients who completed eGFR but are missing only uACR. INCLUDE those rows with `gold_adherence_ked.egfr_flag AND NOT gold_adherence_ked.uacr_flag`. This is distinct from the broad KED care gap filter `gold_adherence_ked.status = 'NOT_MET'`, which includes patients missing eGFR, missing uACR, or missing both. Use the specific filter for “close the uACR gap” outreach and the broad status filter for total KED care gap lists/counts.

snippets.headline: Blood Pressure control measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had a latest reading below 140 over 90.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: BPD means Blood Pressure control for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets BPD when their most recent blood pressure reading is controlled, defined in the instruction as `<140/90`. The standard patient-level BPD compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_bpd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all BPD-eligible rows in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_bpd` at the grouping grain. Use `MEASURE(`BPD Compliance Rate`)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bpd_compliance_metrics` for governed rate reporting.

snippets.headline: Blood Pressure control gaps include both missing readings and uncontrolled latest readings, which support separate outreach lists.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: BPD care gaps split into no-reading gaps and uncontrolled latest-reading gaps. INCLUDE all BPD gap list/count rows with `gold_adherence_bpd.status = 'NOT_MET'`, which covers uncontrolled blood pressure OR no reading. INCLUDE uncontrolled latest-reading gaps and EXCLUDE no-reading gaps with `gold_adherence_bpd.status = 'NOT_MET' AND gold_adherence_bpd.bp_datetime IS NOT NULL`. INCLUDE patients with no BP reading in the measurement year with `gold_adherence_bpd.bp_datetime IS NULL`.

snippets.headline: Eye Exam measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had a retinal or diabetic eye exam during the year.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: EED means Eye Exam for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets EED when they had a retinal or diabetic eye exam in the measurement year, represented by `gold_adherence_eed.numerator_flag`. The standard patient-level EED compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_eed.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all EED-eligible rows at the grouping grain. Use `MEASURE(`EED Compliance Rate`)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.eed_compliance_metrics` for governed rate reporting.

snippets.headline: Unmet adherence records are identified by the single status value NOT_MET across all five care-measure sources.
snippets.source: Query history for eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked
snippets.content: To count adherence gaps, filter each source with the inclusion predicate `status = 'NOT_MET'`; the complete status value used for this gap population is `'NOT_MET'`. The grouped output counts rows as `COUNT(*)` by measure and gap reason, so the patient count is a row count rather than a distinct-patient count. This inclusion rule is applied independently to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd`, `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked`, `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_bpd`, `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd`, and `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_eed`.

snippets.headline: Five adherence measures report whether patients met testing, blood-pressure, statin, and eye-exam care requirements.
snippets.source: Query history for eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked
snippets.content: The adherence reporting domain uses five measure codes: GSD, KED, BPD, SPD, and EED. Across the five physical sources `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd`, `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked`, `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_bpd`, `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd`, and `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_eed`, each row is treated as an eligible patient record because the rate calculation uses `COUNT(*)` as the eligible denominator and `AVG(CAST(numerator_flag AS INT))` as the adherence rate. The source SQL labels the measures as GSD, KED, BPD, SPD, and EED; only the associated care-gap descriptions below are supported by the query text.

snippets.headline: A care gap is a patient-level record marked not met, while met records represent compliant patients.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: In every patient-level gold adherence table, `status = 'NOT_MET'` means the patient has a care gap and `status = 'MET'` means the patient is compliant. To count KED care gaps, use the exact governed query `SELECT COUNT(*) AS ked_care_gaps FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked WHERE status = 'NOT_MET'`. The same status interpretation applies to the corresponding gold adherence tables for GSD, BPD, SPD, and EED.

**CLINIC-04** has the lowest Protocol Step-3 (A1c follow-up) adherence in measurement year 2026. Of its 79 closed high-A1c triggers, 35 (**44.3%**) got a follow-up within 90 days. ### Reading the ranking
- **The bottom three are close.** CLINIC-04 is at 44.3%, CLINIC-07 at 46.5% and CLINIC-01 at 48.1%. Each clinic has only 59–105 triggers, so read the bottom three as one low-performing group rather than a firm last place. ## 1,881 patients have diabetes with kidney complications

That's **62.1%** of the 3,031 patients in the diabetes cohort. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/a48bab2f03744e47a3fe5be7bb0372b7?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_be7107) It's the same number your earlier analyses of this question found. [Diabetes with kidney complications count](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/a6977d55d6f844c39e4c12c0f04a6e0d?o=7474653847172668)

<!-- begin-embedded:query_be7107 -->
| patients_with_kidney_complications | diabetes_cohort_patients | pct_of_cohort | e11_21_nephropathy | e11_22_ckd | e11_29_other_kidney | non_e11_kidney |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1881 | 3031 | 62.1 | 1565 | 1881 | 1032 | 0 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_be7107 -->

**How patients were counted:** each patient counts once if they have any diagnosis in the ICD-10 groups for diabetes with kidney complications: E10.2 (type 1), E11.2 (type 2) or E13.2 (other diabetes). Every code under those groups is included, found through the ICD-10 code hierarchy table. The diabetes cohort is every patient with any diagnosis under E10, E11 or E13. [Diabetes Cohort](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/402e8af3-3e5a-4a46-aa36-22dcd8df5e64?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-6d2030c9-1a4b-4ff7-aa89-ecc48b60f3f9) [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/silver_condition?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/icd10_closure?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

**By code** (many patients have more than one code, so these numbers don't add up to the total):
- **E11.22, diabetic chronic kidney disease:** 1,881 patients. Every patient in the group has this code.
- **E11.21, diabetic nephropathy:** 1,565 patients
- **E11.29, other diabetic kidney complication:** 1,032 patients

All of these kidney codes are type 2 diabetes (E11) codes. The data has no type 1 or other-diabetes kidney codes.

This is a diagnosis count. It is not the HEDIS kidney health evaluation (KED) measure, which checks whether diabetic patients aged 18–85 had both an eGFR test and a uACR test. [KED (Kidney Health Evaluation)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/2917aa8e-38e0-48a0-90b5-040c2931541a?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) The data is synthetic demo data that follows HEDIS but isn't NCQA-certified.
genie_one_sql:
WITH dm AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.`patient_id`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`silver_condition` c
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_closure` h
    ON c.`icd10_code` = h.`descendant_code` AND h.`ancestor_code` IN ('E10','E11','E13')),
kid AS (
  SELECT c.`patient_id`, c.`icd10_code`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`silver_condition` c
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_closure` h
    ON c.`icd10_code` = h.`descendant_code` AND h.`ancestor_code` IN ('E10.2','E11.2','E13.2'))
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT `patient_id`) FROM kid) AS patients_with_kidney_complications,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dm) AS diabetes_cohort_patients,
  ROUND(100.0 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT `patient_id`) FROM kid) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dm), 1) AS pct_of_cohort,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT `patient_id`) FROM kid WHERE `icd10_code`='E11.21') AS e11_21_nephropathy,

snippets.headline: Glycemic control rates measure results among tested patients, while Glycemic Status compliance measures testing among all eligible patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For GSD, good and poor glycemic control rates are computed only among A1c-tested patients, not all eligible diabetic patients. The good control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, where the denominator is the count of tested patients. The poor control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_gt9) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, using the same tested-patient denominator. This differs from GSD compliance rate, whose denominator is all eligible GSD patients: `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`.

snippets.headline: Glycemic Status Assessment measures whether eligible diabetic patients aged 18–75 had an A1c test during the year.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment for diabetic patients aged 18-75. A patient meets GSD when they have an A1c test in the measurement year, represented in patient detail by `gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag`. The standard patient-level compliance formula is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`, where the denominator is all eligible rows in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd` at the grouping grain. pages_read.body:
## Definition
HEDIS measure of whether patients with diabetes had their glycemic status (**HbA1c**) assessed during the measurement year.

## Measure specification
* **Denominator:** **Diabetes Cohort**, aged **18–75** at the end of the measurement year.
* **Numerator:** at least one HbA1c test in the measurement year.
* **Value set:** `GSD_A1C_TEST`
* **Control bands (latest A1c):** good control **< 8%**, poor control **> 9%**.

## Data
* **Metric:** `GSD Compliance Rate` in `gsd_compliance_metrics`
* **Patient-level detail:** `gold_adherence_gsd` (MET / NOT_MET with test evidence)

---
_GSD replaces the older "HbA1c Control for Patients With Diabetes" framing. HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified._

## GSD poor-control rate: A1c-tested patients only, poor control means A1c above 9%

The poor-control rate counts **only patients who had an A1c test** in the measurement year, not all eligible patients. A patient is in poor control when their **latest A1c is above 9%**. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-96a50ca6-4d7e-49f5-9be7-959c98fc976b) [GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/1045ab28-3390-4c2f-a056-381c1019c345?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) This is the same answer you got in your earlier sessions. I checked it again against the current definitions and nothing has changed. [Earlier GSD poor-control question](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d78ea599983c4eeb891eff3f8557bc6b?o=7474653847172668)

| Metric | Who it counts | Who meets it |
|---|---|---|
| GSD compliance rate | All eligible GSD patients (diabetes, age 18–75) | Had at least one A1c test in the year |
| Good-control rate | A1c-tested patients only | Latest A1c **below 8%** |
| Poor-control rate | A1c-tested patients only | Latest A1c **above 9%** |

[Knowledge snippet](#snippet-5a6324fb-8fbe-4a26-abd6-1a0ebcc5cd00) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-93568b56-c797-4116-8166-db6fa073557b)

**What this means in practice**
- Patients fall into four groups: *Not tested*, *Good (<8%)*, *Moderate (8–9%)* and *Poor (>9%)*. "Not tested" means the patient missed the test, not that their A1c is at some level. That's why untested patients are left out of the poor-control rate. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-d32dc0bb-67e2-402a-9aaf-ffe1f3a5ca0c)
- So a clinic that tests few patients can still show a low poor-control rate. Read it next to the compliance (testing) rate.
- A separate glossary page, "Poorly controlled diabetes," uses the same >9% cutoff. But it divides by **all** patients with diabetes, not just tested ones, so don't swap the two definitions. [Poorly controlled diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/89de86e4-4d18-4848-9c16-cfa8b107ba8b?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- The protocol's Step-3 A1c follow-up uses a different, lower cutoff (**A1c ≥ 7%**). That cutoff decides who needs a follow-up; it isn't a measure of poor control. [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

This is demo content modeled on HEDIS, not NCQA-certified. Hospice, ESRD (end-stage renal disease) and frailty exclusions aren't applied, so the count of eligible patients runs slightly high. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-a5cf6b49-638b-4371-a06e-271d331c3089) [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

The good control rate is `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.a1c_lt8) / COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag)`, where the denominator is the count of tested patients. This differs from GSD compliance rate, whose denominator is all eligible GSD patients: `COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.numerator_flag) / COUNT(*)`.

pages_read.body:
## Definition
HEDIS measure of kidney-health evaluation in patients with diabetes. Its numerator is **compound**: it requires two different lab tests in the same year.

## Measure specification
* **Denominator:** **Diabetes Cohort**, aged **18–85** at the end of the measurement year.
* **Numerator:** **both** an **eGFR** test and a **uACR** test in the measurement year. Missing either one is a care gap.
* **Value sets:** `KED_EGFR`, `KED_UACR`

## Data
* **Metrics** in `ked_compliance_metrics`: `KED Compliance Rate` (combined), `eGFR Test Rate`, `uACR Test Rate`
* **Patient-level detail:** `gold_adherence_ked` (`egfr_flag`, `uacr_flag`)

## Examples
Demo rates: eGFR \~92%, uACR \~51%, combined \~51%. The combined rate tracks uACR.

---
_KED is the worked example for Measure Drift (eGFR code versions). HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified._

## KED: who's eligible and what counts as compliant

**Who's eligible:** patients in the **Diabetes Cohort** who are **18–85 years old at the end of the measurement year (December 31)**. The Diabetes Cohort is anyone with an ICD-10-CM diagnosis under E10, E11 or E13, including all child codes. [KED (Kidney Health Evaluation)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/2917aa8e-38e0-48a0-90b5-040c2931541a?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Diabetes Cohort](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/402e8af3-3e5a-4a46-aa36-22dcd8df5e64?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/gold_adherence_ked?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

**What counts as compliant:** the patient needs **both** of these tests in the same measurement year:
1. an **eGFR** test (code list `KED_EGFR`: LOINC 33914-3 MDRD or 98979-8 CKD-EPI), **and**
2. a **uACR** test (code list `KED_UACR`, e.g. 14959-1, the microalbumin/creatinine ratio).

Having only one of the two tests is a care gap. There's no partial credit. [eGFR (Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/150dfd59-85b9-4efd-8014-bb170bfe626e?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-d3494f59-4cda-47e7-babd-761d66786d55) [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

KED covers older patients than the related measures. GSD and the eye exam stop at 75, and SPD covers ages 40–75, so patients aged 76–85 appear only in KED. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-58db899b-2b13-4088-b3cf-5974272cc9a7) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-670bc59e-4126-4b88-9bdb-91dd8161a367)

## What the current data shows

[query not found in registry: 01f1d1da-8f3a-18df-a97a-dd854f74b9f1]

- **2,802 patients are eligible** in measurement year 2026, aged 18–85.
- **1,327 of them (47.4%) are compliant.** 87.5% had an eGFR test, but only 47.4% had a uACR test. The overall rate matches the uACR rate exactly, so **uACR testing is what holds the rate down**.
- Of the 1,475 patients with a gap, **1,126 are missing only the uACR test** and 349 are missing both tests. No one is missing only eGFR. The quickest gains would come from ordering uACR for patients who already had an eGFR. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-88f7efad-178c-4e90-8b3e-82284084bb1a)

The table doesn't currently have its `status` or compliance flag columns. Instead, I counted a test as done if it has a result date in the year, which is the same approach as your earlier KED analysis. [Prior KED eligibility analysis](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/e2dae179872f4004be0bd109c6af9172?o=7474653847172668)

*This is HEDIS-aligned demo data, not NCQA-certified. Hospice, ESRD and frailty exclusions aren't applied, so the eligible count runs slightly high.*

SELECT `measurement_year`, COUNT(DISTINCT `patient_id`) AS eligible_patients, MIN(`age`) AS min_age, MAX(`age`) AS max_age,
COUNT_IF(`egfr_datetime` IS NOT NULL AND `uacr_datetime` IS NOT NULL) AS compliant,
ROUND(100*COUNT_IF(`egfr_datetime` IS NOT NULL AND `uacr_datetime` IS NOT NULL)/COUNT(*),1) AS ked_rate_pct,
ROUND(100*COUNT_IF(`egfr_datetime` IS NOT NULL)/COUNT(*),1) AS egfr_rate_pct,

COUNT_IF(`egfr_datetime` IS NULL AND `uacr_datetime` IS NOT NULL) AS missing_egfr_only,

FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_ked` WHERE `eligible_flag` GROUP BY `measurement_year` ORDER BY `measurement_year`

## 198 statin patients have a diagnosis the care protocol lists as a statin contraindication

**198 patients** have a statin order and also have one of their own diagnoses on the care protocol's statin contraindication list. That's about 4% of the **4,741 patients with any statin order**. All 198 match on **pregnancy**. None match on hepatic disease. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/140bddd06ccf404bb9b491059d747a77?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_9dd18a)

### The protocol rules
The care protocol lists two statin contraindications, both from the section labeled "CP sec4":

<!-- begin-embedded:query_11d329 -->
| subject | predicate | object | source | icd10_codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DRUGCLASS-STATIN | contraindicatedWith | CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | O15, Z34, O26, O00 |
| DRUGCLASS-STATIN | contraindicatedWith | CONTRA_HEPATIC | CP sec4 | K70, K74 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_11d329 -->

### How patients were matched
- **Statin orders:** I mapped each ordered product up to the statin drug class. Checking the main medication orders table and the adjusted medication table gives the same 4,741 patients and the same 198 matches. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/140bddd06ccf404bb9b491059d747a77?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_7ec9f8)
- **Diagnoses:** I checked each patient's own encounter diagnoses against the diagnosis codes for each rule, including the more specific codes under each one. [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- These are the same steps as your earlier runs of this question, and the result hasn't changed. [Prior statin contraindication count](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/fae0f5057a2d422ba2a6b3ad47c331eb?o=7474653847172668)

### Narrower definitions give smaller counts
The protocol rule doesn't set a time window, so the 198 includes matching diagnoses from any date. Many of these pregnancies were recorded years before the statin was ordered.

| Definition | Patients |
|---|---|
| Matching diagnosis at any time (the protocol as written) | **198** |
| Diagnosis recorded on or after the first statin order | 94 |
| Diagnosis during the statin order period, or in the 280 days (about one pregnancy) before it | 80 |

[Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/140bddd06ccf404bb9b491059d747a77?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_9dd18a)

The **80 patients** whose pregnancy falls during or just before their statin orders are the best group for clinical review.

**Caveats:**
- "Prescribed a statin" here means a statin order was placed at some point. It doesn't mean the statin is currently active or was dispensed.
- Pregnancy end dates aren't recorded, so the two time-based counts are estimates.
- This is synthetic demo data aligned to HEDIS standards, not certified by NCQA. The statin-therapy (SPD) measure tables don't exclude patients for these contraindications.

WITH rx_orders AS (
  SELECT m.`patient_id`, m.`start_ts`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`bronze_order_med` m
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`rxnorm_closure` cls ON m.`rxnorm_code` = cls.`descendant_code` AND cls.`ancestor_code` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
),
rx AS (SELECT `patient_id`, MIN(`start_ts`) AS first_ts, MAX(`start_ts`) AS last_ts FROM rx_orders GROUP BY `patient_id`),
rule AS (SELECT DISTINCT `object` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` WHERE `subject` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND `predicate` = 'contraindicatedWith'),
vs AS (SELECT DISTINCT `segment_id`, `code` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`value_set_segment` WHERE `code_system` = 'ICD10CM'),
hits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.`patient_id`, rule.`object` AS contra, d.`onset_date`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`bronze_pat_enc_dx` d
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_closure` c ON d.`icd10_code` = c.`descendant_code`
  JOIN vs ON vs.`code` = c.`ancestor_code`
  JOIN rule ON rule.`object` = vs.`segment_id`
  WHERE d.`patient_id` IN (SELECT `patient_id` FROM rx)
),
p AS (
  SELECT h.`patient_id`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN contra='CONTRA_PREGNANCY' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) preg,
    MAX(CASE WHEN contra='CONTRA_HEPATIC' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) hep,
    MAX(CASE WHEN h.`onset_date` BETWEEN date_sub(CAST(rx.first_ts AS DATE), 280) AND CAST(rx.last_ts AS DATE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) overlap_statin_period,
    MAX(CASE WHEN h.`onset_date` >= CAST(rx.first_ts AS DATE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) dx_after_first_statin
  FROM hits h JOIN rx ON rx.`patient_id` = h.`patient_id` GROUP BY h.`patient_id`
)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rx) AS patients_with_statin_order,
  COUNT(*) AS statin_pts_with_contraindicating_dx,
  SUM(preg) AS with_pregnancy_dx, SUM(hep) AS with_hepatic_dx, SUM(preg*hep) AS with_both,
  SUM(dx_after_first_statin) AS dx_onset_on_or_after_first_statin_order,
  SUM(overlap_statin_period) AS dx_within_statin_order_span_incl_280d_lookback
FROM p

SELECT e.`subject`, e.`predicate`, e.`object`, e.`source`, concat_ws(', ', collect_set(v.`code`)) AS icd10_codes
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` e
LEFT JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`value_set_segment` v ON v.`segment_id` = e.`object` AND v.`code_system` = 'ICD10CM'
WHERE e.`subject` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND e.`predicate` LIKE 'contraindicated%'
GROUP BY ALL

WITH rx AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.`patient_id`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`care_order_med` m
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`rxnorm_closure` cls ON m.`rxnorm_code` = cls.`descendant_code` AND cls.`ancestor_code` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
),
rule AS (SELECT DISTINCT `object` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` WHERE `subject` = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND `predicate` = 'contraindicatedWith'),
vs AS (SELECT DISTINCT `segment_id`, `code` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`value_set_segment` WHERE `code_system` = 'ICD10CM'),
hits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.`patient_id`
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`bronze_pat_enc_dx` d
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_closure` c ON d.`icd10_code` = c.`descendant_code`
  JOIN vs ON vs.`code` = c.`ancestor_code`
  JOIN rule ON rule.`object` = vs.`segment_id`
)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rx) AS patients_with_statin_order,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rx JOIN hits USING (`patient_id`)) AS statin_pts_with_contraindicating_dx

## E11.22 rolls up to two top-level conditions

E11.22 (*Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease*) has two direct parents, so it sits under two top-level conditions: **E11 – Type 2 diabetes mellitus** and **N18 – Chronic kidney disease (CKD)**. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/2ca4b7221e624ea38f030c508c61765b?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_2a094b) [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_hier](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/icd10_hier?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

| Top-level condition | Path from E11.22 | Levels up |
|---|---|---|
| **E11** – Type 2 diabetes mellitus | E11.22 → **E11.2** (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with kidney complications) → E11 | 2 |
| **N18** – Chronic kidney disease | E11.22 → N18 (direct parent, no code in between) | 1 |

[Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/2ca4b7221e624ea38f030c508c61765b?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_43e918)

**What this means for analysis:** because of the two parents, an E11.22 diagnosis is picked up by three subtree searches in the ancestor/descendant lookup table: the diabetes cohort (E11), kidney complications (E11.2) and CKD (N18). [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/icd10_closure?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-6d2030c9-1a4b-4ff7-aa89-ecc48b60f3f9) [hedis-diabetes-quality](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/tools/skills/%2FWorkspace%2FUsers%2Feli.swanson%40databricks.com%2F.assistant%2Fskills%2Fhedis-diabetes-quality?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) A filter that only matches codes starting with "N18" would miss these patients when counting CKD.

This hierarchy is a curated demo subset focused on diabetes, so neither E11 nor N18 has a chapter-level parent above it here. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_hier](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/icd10_hier?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

SELECT c.`ancestor_code`, c.`ancestor_name`, c.`depth`,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_hier` h WHERE h.`code` = c.`ancestor_code` AND h.`parent_code` IS NOT NULL AND h.`parent_code` <> '') AS n_parents
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_closure` c
WHERE c.`descendant_code` = 'E11.22'
ORDER BY c.`depth`, c.`ancestor_code`

WITH RECURSIVE up (code, parent_code, path, lvl) AS (
  SELECT `code`, `parent_code`, CAST(`code` AS STRING), 0 FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_hier` WHERE `code` = 'E11.22'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT h.`code`, h.`parent_code`, CONCAT(u.path, ' → ', h.`code`), u.lvl + 1
  FROM up u JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_hier` h ON h.`code` = u.parent_code
  WHERE u.lvl < 10
)
SELECT path, code AS last_code, parent_code FROM up ORDER BY path

| CLINIC-06 | 74 | 44 | 59.5 | 31 | 51.0 |
| CLINIC-08 | 105 | 63 | 60.0 | 37 | 48.0 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_7d548e -->

### What stands out
- **The lead is small.** CLINIC-07 is next at 46.5%, about 2 points higher. With only 59–105 obligations per clinic, a gap that size could close quickly.
- **The problem is missed follow-ups, not slow ones.** When CLINIC-04 does follow up, it takes about 48 days on average, which is in line with the other clinics (46–51 days).
- **CLINIC-04's rate can still change.** It has 24 more obligations whose 90-day windows are still open, so those patients can still get their follow-up this year.
- Clinic rates range from 44.3% (CLINIC-04) to 60.0% (CLINIC-08).

### How the rate is measured
This uses the same certified metric view as your earlier analyses. [Prior Step-3 clinic analysis](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/19f17353965647f8b53d207314a342cc?o=3464092709171785)
- **An obligation** is an A1c result of 9% or higher whose 90-day follow-up window has closed.
- **The step is met** when a follow-up A1c happens within those 90 days.
- **Windows still open aren't counted.** Counting them would include early successes before any misses are known, which would make the rate look better than it is.

The certified HEDIS Diabetes Quality Genie space covers only the six HEDIS measures, not this protocol step, so I queried the metric view directly. This is a demo measure aligned with HEDIS. It is not certified by NCQA.

FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_semantic`.`protocol_adherence_metrics`
WHERE `Measurement Year` = 2026
GROUP BY ALL

## 1,881 patients have diabetes with kidney complications

**1,881 patients** in the care protocol condition data have a diagnosis code for diabetes with kidney complications. That's **62.1% of the 3,031 patients with diabetes**. [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7a97c70f46da4b27b6fbe68dee83e374?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_a15cca) [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/silver_condition?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

<!-- begin-embedded:query_a15cca -->
| diabetic_patients | patients_with_diabetic_kidney_code_E1x_2x | diabetic_patients_with_ckd_N18 | either_definition | pct_of_diabetics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3031 | 1881 | 1791 | 1881 | 62.1 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_a15cca -->

### How the count is defined
- **Diabetes with kidney complications** means any ICD-10 code under E10.2x, E11.2x or E13.2x. Only type 2 codes (E11.2x) show up in the data. The diabetes group is every patient with any code under E10, E11 or E13. I used the same method as your earlier conversation on this question, and the result is the same. [Earlier diabetes and kidney count](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/4b78ea9e654444338d1cb67eb85d628d?o=3464092709171785)
- **Checked against chronic kidney disease (CKD) codes:** 1,791 diabetic patients also have a separate CKD code (N18.x). All of them already have a diabetic kidney code, so counting patients who meet either definition still gives 1,881.

### Breakdown by diagnosis code
- All 1,881 patients have the code for kidney disorder due to diabetes (E11.22).
- 1,565 have microalbuminuria due to diabetes (E11.21) and 1,032 have proteinuria due to diabetes (E11.29).
- CKD stages range from stage 1 (1,672 patients) to end-stage renal disease (75 patients).
- Many patients have more than one code, so these counts overlap and can't be added together.

<!-- begin-embedded:query_751201 -->
| icd10_code | description | patients |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E11.22 | Disorder of kidney due to diabetes mellitus (disorder) | 1881 |
| N18.1 | Chronic kidney disease stage 1 (disorder) | 1672 |
| E11.21 | Microalbuminuria due to type 2 diabetes mellitus (disorder) | 1565 |
| N18.2 | Chronic kidney disease stage 2 (disorder) | 1427 |
| E11.29 | Proteinuria due to type 2 diabetes mellitus (disorder) | 1032 |
| N18.30 | Chronic kidney disease stage 3 (disorder) | 891 |
| N18.4 | Chronic kidney disease stage 4 (disorder) | 421 |
| N18.6 | End-stage renal disease (disorder) | 75 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_751201 -->

These counts include anyone who has ever had one of these diagnoses. They aren't limited to a date range or to conditions that are still active.
genie_one_sql:
WITH p AS (
  SELECT `patient_id`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `icd10_code` RLIKE '^E1[013]\\.2' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dkd_code,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `icd10_code` RLIKE '^E1[013]' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS diabetes,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `icd10_code` LIKE 'N18%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ckd
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`silver_condition`
  GROUP BY `patient_id`)
SELECT
  SUM(diabetes) AS diabetic_patients,
  SUM(dkd_code) AS patients_with_diabetic_kidney_code_E1x_2x,
  SUM(CASE WHEN diabetes=1 AND ckd=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS diabetic_patients_with_ckd_N18,
  SUM(CASE WHEN dkd_code=1 OR (diabetes=1 AND ckd=1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS either_definition,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(dkd_code)/SUM(diabetes),1) AS pct_of_diabetics
FROM p

SELECT `icd10_code`, `description`, COUNT(DISTINCT `patient_id`) AS patients
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`silver_condition`
WHERE `icd10_code` RLIKE '^(E1[013]\\.2|N18)'
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY patients DESC

onto_poor_control_denominator.genie_one_answer:
## GSD Poor Control Rate: only A1c-tested patients, with poor control meaning A1c above 9.0%

**It uses only some of the eligible patients.** The denominator is eligible patients who had **at least one A1c test in the measurement year**. A patient counts as poorly controlled when their **latest A1c in the measurement year is above 9.0%**. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_semantic/gsd_compliance_metrics?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785) This is the same answer as last time, and the definitions are unchanged. [Earlier GSD poor-control question](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/bc616bf838804e2c8acd436b9da69602?o=3464092709171785)

### How the GSD metric view defines it (certified)
- **Poor Control Rate** = Poor Control Patients ÷ patients who had an A1c test. Eligible patients with no test this year are not counted. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_semantic/gsd_compliance_metrics?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)
- **Poor control** means the latest A1c is **> 9.0%**. The cutoff is strict, so a reading of exactly 9.0% doesn't count.
- **Good control** means the latest A1c is **< 8.0%**. Readings from 8.0% to 9.0% are in neither group. [GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment)](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/1045ab28-3390-4c2f-a056-381c1019c345?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)
- **Eligible patients** are diabetes patients aged **18–75** at the end of the measurement year. They are the base for the separate **GSD Compliance Rate** (the share who were tested). [GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment)](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/1045ab28-3390-4c2f-a056-381c1019c345?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

### Why it matters
Untested patients are left out of the poor-control rate completely. When testing rates are low, the rate can look better than the real picture, so read it alongside the GSD Compliance Rate.

**Watch for a different definition:** an uncertified glossary page, "Poorly controlled diabetes," uses a wider base: all health-center patients with diabetes whose latest HbA1c is above 9%. [Poorly controlled diabetes](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/89de86e4-4d18-4848-9c16-cfa8b107ba8b?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785) For GSD reporting, use the certified metric view's definition.

snippets.headline: Eligibility driven amendment rate is the fraction of protocol amendments caused by eligibility criteria changes.
snippets.source: test clinical trial space
snippets.content: Eligibility Driven Amendment Rate in `eswanson_demo.clinical_trials.protocol_amendment_metrics` is the share of all amendments classified as Eligibility Criteria changes on a 0–1 scale. Compute it as `MEASURE(`Eligibility Criteria Amendment Count`) / NULLIF(MEASURE(`Total Amendments`), 0)` at the selected grouping grain, such as `Trial Phase`. The numerator is eligibility-criteria amendment count, and the denominator is total amendments for the same group. Do not interpret the result as a percentage unless explicitly multiplying by 100.

snippets.headline: Protocol amendment categories are distinct and must match the specific amendment burden question being answered.
snippets.source: test clinical trial space
snippets.content: Protocol amendment type analysis in `eswanson_demo.clinical_trials.protocol_amendment_metrics` separates amendment categories into distinct measures: `MEASURE(`Eligibility Criteria Amendment Count`)`, `MEASURE(`Safety Update Amendment Count`)`, `MEASURE(`Dose Modification Amendment Count`)`, and `MEASURE(`Statistical Plan Amendment Count`)`. A standard indication-level profile groups by `Trial Indication` and reports all four category counts plus `MEASURE(`Total Amendments`)`, sorted by total amendments descending. These category counts are adjacent but not interchangeable: eligibility criteria changes support eligibility-driven amendment rate, safety update changes support safety amendment rate, dose modification changes are separate from safety update numerator in the provided safety-rate query, and statistical plan changes are their own amendment category. Use the category measure matching the business question rather than summing or substituting another category.

snippets.headline: Metabolic abnormality comparisons by insurance require more than twenty patients with any lab result.
snippets.source: test space
snippets.content: For metabolic abnormality comparisons by primary insurance in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics`, the curated query suppresses small denominators. Include only insurance groups where `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Any Lab Result`) > 20`. The numerator-like companion measure is `MEASURE(`Unique Patients with Abnormal Metabolic Results`)`, and the rate is `MEASURE(`High and Critically High Metabolic Lab Result Patient Rate`)`. The exact threshold is `> 20`, and it is applied with `HAVING` after grouping by `Primary Insurance`.

snippets.headline: Serious adverse events count CTCAE grade three or higher events and are normalized by enrolled patients.
snippets.source: test clinical trial space
snippets.content: Serious Adverse Events are defined as adverse events with CTCAE grade `>= 3`. In `eswanson_demo.clinical_trials.trial_portfolio_metrics`, use `MEASURE(`Serious Adverse Event Count`)` for the serious adverse event numerator. For sponsor-level serious adverse event burden per enrolled patient, compute `MEASURE(`Serious Adverse Event Count`) / NULLIF(MEASURE(`Enrolled Patient Count`), 0)` and apply `HAVING MEASURE(`Enrolled Patient Count`) > 0` to avoid zero-denominator groups. The denominator is enrolled patients aggregated at the same grouping grain, such as sponsor or biomarker-stratification status, not the number of trials.

snippets.headline: Encounters per Patient shows encounter intensity by dividing encounter volume by unique patients in the same segment.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics
snippets.content: `Encounters per Patient` in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics` is an average utilization intensity measure at the selected dimension grain. Its queryable expression is ``MEASURE(`Encounters per Patient`)``; the definition-time expression over the source is `COUNT(1) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT source.patient_key), 0)`. The numerator is total encounters and the denominator is distinct patients within the same selected grouping, not calendar days or all patients in the system. Use this named measure rather than dividing `MEASURE(`Encounter Count`)` by `MEASURE(`Patient Count`)` unless you intentionally need equivalent arithmetic outside the measure calls at the same grain.

snippets.headline: Base count measures distinguish line records from unique sales, customers, products, and dates.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.slp_demo.sales_metrics
snippets.content: `record_count`, `distinct_sale`, `distinct_customer`, `distinct_product`, and `distinct_date` in `eswanson_demo.slp_demo.sales_metrics` are the base count measures used as denominators in derived metrics. Query them as `MEASURE(`record_count`)`, `MEASURE(`distinct_sale`)`, `MEASURE(`distinct_customer`)`, `MEASURE(`distinct_product`)`, and `MEASURE(`distinct_date`)`; their definition-time source expressions are `COUNT(1)`, `COUNT(DISTINCT sale_id)`, `COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)`, `COUNT(DISTINCT product_id)`, and `COUNT(DISTINCT date_key)`. `record_count` counts sales records or line items, while the distinct measures count unique sale, customer, product, or date values within the grouped result. These counts answer different denominator questions and should not be substituted for each other in per-customer, per-sale, per-product, or per-day calculations.

snippets.headline: The deceased status rate identifies inactive patients who would inflate active-population allergy and care-gap reporting.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.metadata_results.allergy_metrics
snippets.content: `Active Patient Deceased Status Exclusion Rate` is defined as `SUM(CASE WHEN patient.patient_status = 'Deceased' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT source.pat_id), 0)`. The numerator counts allergy-population rows where the joined patient dimension has `patient.patient_status = 'Deceased'`, while the denominator is distinct patients with allergy records (`COUNT(DISTINCT source.pat_id)`). The measure is intended as a quality/control indicator to ensure active-population metrics and care gap reports are not inflated by patients flagged as deceased; if computing active-population allergy metrics directly, analysts should EXCLUDE `patient.patient_status = 'Deceased'`.

snippets.headline: Insurance Coverage Rate shows the charge-weighted share of charges paid by insurance within each segment.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics
snippets.content: `Insurance Coverage Rate` in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics` measures the fraction of total charges covered by insurance in the selected grouping. Its queryable expression is ``MEASURE(`Insurance Coverage Rate`)``; the definition-time expression over the source is `SUM(source.insurance_paid) / NULLIF(SUM(source.total_charges), 0)`. The numerator is summed insurance-paid amount and the denominator is summed total charges over the same grouping; this is a charge-weighted rate, not an average of encounter-level coverage percentages. Use it for payer-mix and coverage analysis by `Primary Insurance`, demographic dimensions, encounter type, or month.

snippets.headline: Length-of-stay and ICU quantities are whole days, and financial amounts are United States dollars.
snippets.source: clinical_genie_space_mvs
snippets.content: LOS and ICU day measures in this Genie space are measured in whole days, while charges and payments are measured in USD. This unit rule applies when interpreting `MEASURE(`Total LOS Days`)`, ICU utilization metrics, `MEASURE(`Total Charges`)`, `MEASURE(`Total Insurance Paid`)`, and `MEASURE(`Total Patient Paid`)`. Do not interpret LOS or ICU measures as hours, and do not mix financial measures with non-USD currencies in downstream calculations.

The same demographic fields in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.encounter_metrics` and `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.clinical_event_metrics` should be used only when the population is explicitly scoped to encounters or lab/clinical events. This prevents mixing a patient denominator with an encounter or event numerator.

The inclusion list is exactly `Event Description IN ('Glucose', 'Hemoglobin A1C')`; no other lab event descriptions are part of the metabolic lab flag definition in this Genie space. snippets.content: Emergency encounter share is computed in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.encounter_metrics` as `MEASURE(`Emergency Encounter Count`) / NULLIF(MEASURE(`Total Encounters`), 0)`. snippets.headline: Patient Responsibility Rate shows the charge-weighted share of charges paid by patients within each segment.
snippets.source: eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics
snippets.content: `Patient Responsibility Rate` in `eswanson_demo.epic_emr_demo.patient_demographics_metrics` measures the fraction of total charges borne by the patient in the selected grouping. Its queryable expression is ``MEASURE(`Patient Responsibility Rate`)``; the definition-time expression over the source is `SUM(source.patient_paid) / NULLIF(SUM(source.total_charges), 0)`. The numerator is summed patient-paid amount and the denominator is summed total charges over the same grouping; this is a charge-weighted rate, not an average of row-level patient responsibility percentages. Use it to compare patient financial responsibility across demographics, payer segments, encounter types, or months.

pages_read.body:
**KED (Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes)** is a HEDIS quality measure for assessing kidney
health in diabetic patients. Its numerator is **compound** — it requires two different tests in the same year.

- **Eligible population (denominator):** patients aged **18–85** as of the end of the measurement year in the
  **diabetes cohort**.
- **Numerator (compliant):** **both** of the following in the measurement year:
  1. an **eGFR** (estimated glomerular filtration rate) test — value set `KED_EGFR`, and
  2. a **uACR** (urine albumin-creatinine ratio) test — value set `KED_UACR`.

A patient is **MET** only when **both** components are present; missing either is a care gap. Because the two
components are tracked separately, the **eGFR Test Rate** and **uACR Test Rate** are each exposed in
`ked_compliance_metrics` alongside the combined **KED Compliance Rate**. In this demo uACR is the limiting
component (eGFR ~92%, uACR ~51%, combined ~51%).

> The eGFR value set spans LOINC vintages (e.g. `33914-3` MDRD and `98979-8`) — a reminder that value sets
> evolve and a measure must accept all valid codes for the concept. HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified.

## Definition
The set of patients with a diabetes diagnosis: any ICD-10-CM code that is a **descendant of E10, E11, or E13** (type 1, type 2, and other/specified diabetes).

## How it is resolved
The cohort is resolved semantically, not from a hand-maintained code list. `silver_condition` is joined to `icd10_closure` on `descendant_code` where `ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13')`. One equality join captures the whole subtree (e.g. `E11.21`, `E11.319`); see **Code Subsumption**.

## Data
`silver_diabetes_cohort`: one row per distinct `patient_id`.

## Business use
All five diabetes measures apply their own age band to this cohort. A flat code list would miss specific child codes and undercount every measure.

## KED (Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients With Diabetes)

**Who is eligible:** patients in the **diabetes cohort** who are **18–85 years old at the end of the measurement year**. :citation[knowledge_page.9edbb1f7-62bd-405e-9bb6-fa9413b7d243] [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/gold_adherence_ked?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)

2. at least one **uACR** (urine albumin-creatinine ratio) test (value set `KED_UACR`).

If either test is missing, the patient doesn't count as compliant and that missing test is a care gap. :citation[knowledge_page.9edbb1f7-62bd-405e-9bb6-fa9413b7d243]

## 198 patients have a statin order despite a contraindicating diagnosis

**198 patients** have a statin order and also have at least one diagnosis of their own that the care protocol lists as a statin contraindication. That's about 4% of the 4,741 patients with a statin order. All 198 fall under the protocol's **pregnancy** rule (section 4 of the care protocol says statins should not be used during pregnancy). [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/878f358f4f82418da3e67ae6562b8518?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_a76561) [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/878f358f4f82418da3e67ae6562b8518?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_ac06e8)

<!-- begin-embedded:query_3c0053 -->
| contraindication | protocol_rule | icd10_code | diagnosis | patients | statins |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | Z34.90 | Normal pregnancy (finding) | 198 | atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, simvastatin |
| CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | O00.1 | Tubal pregnancy (disorder) | 10 | atorvastatin, simvastatin |
| CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | O15.9 | Eclampsia in pregnancy (disorder) | 10 | simvastatin |
| CONTRA_PREGNANCY | CP sec4 | O26.9 | Complication occurring during pregnancy (disorder) | 2 | atorvastatin, simvastatin |
<!-- end-embedded:query_3c0053 -->

- **Every one of the 198 has "Normal pregnancy" on their record.** Some also have a tubal pregnancy (10), eclampsia (10) or another pregnancy complication (2). Some patients have more than one of these diagnoses, so the rows in the table add up to more than 198.
- **The statins involved are atorvastatin, rosuvastatin and simvastatin.**
- **No one is flagged under the liver-disease rule.** The protocol also says statins should not be used with liver disease, but none of the patients on a statin have a liver-disease diagnosis.
- **Same answer as earlier runs.** Earlier runs of this question with the same method also found 198. [Statin contraindication count](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/02fee06681b14c8eaf8f47ba1fc2cd05?o=3464092709171785)

### How patients were matched
Each statin order is first linked to the statin drug class. The protocol's two rules for that class (pregnancy and liver disease) each come with a list of diagnosis codes. Those lists are then checked against every code on the patient's record, including more specific codes that fall under a listed code.

### What the 198 doesn't tell you
The check only asks whether the diagnosis appears anywhere on the patient's record. It doesn't check whether the pregnancy and the statin order happened at the same time. When one of these patients was reviewed in an earlier conversation, the pregnancy had been recorded years before the statin was ordered. [Statin contraindication count](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d9d9268db6494552924b139cef4e3036?o=3464092709171785) So 198 is the number of patients the rule flags. The number with a real overlap is probably lower, so a clinician should review these patients before treating them as current conflicts.
genie_one_sql: SELECT * FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges WHERE subject = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' OR object = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'

WITH statin_rx AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med m
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc
    ON rc.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code AND rc.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'),
contra AS (
  SELECT pe.object AS segment_id, pe.source, vs.code
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges pe
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment vs
    ON vs.segment_id = pe.object AND vs.code_system = 'ICD10CM'
  WHERE pe.subject = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND pe.predicate = 'contraindicatedWith'),
via_closure AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT sc.patient_id, c.segment_id
  FROM statin_rx s
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition sc ON sc.patient_id = s.patient_id
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure ic ON ic.descendant_code = sc.icd10_code
  JOIN contra c ON c.code = ic.ancestor_code)
SELECT segment_id, COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS patients FROM via_closure GROUP BY ALL
UNION ALL SELECT 'ANY contraindication', COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM via_closure
UNION ALL SELECT 'All statin patients', COUNT(*) FROM statin_rx

WITH rx AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.patient_id, rc2.ancestor_name AS statin_ingredient
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med m
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc ON rc.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code AND rc.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure rc2 ON rc2.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code AND rc2.depth > 0 AND rc2.ancestor_code <> 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'),
contra AS (
  SELECT pe.object AS segment_id, pe.source, vs.code
  FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges pe
  JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment vs ON vs.segment_id = pe.object AND vs.code_system = 'ICD10CM'
  WHERE pe.subject = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND pe.predicate = 'contraindicatedWith')
SELECT c.segment_id AS contraindication, c.source AS protocol_rule, sc.icd10_code, sc.description AS diagnosis,
       COUNT(DISTINCT rx.patient_id) AS patients,
       concat_ws(', ', array_sort(collect_set(rx.statin_ingredient))) AS statins
FROM rx
JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition sc ON sc.patient_id = rx.patient_id
JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure ic ON ic.descendant_code = sc.icd10_code
JOIN contra c ON c.code = ic.ancestor_code
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY patients DESC

## Definition
**Subsumption** is the "is-a" relationship between a broader concept and its narrower descendants. For example, `E11.21` *Type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy* **is a** `E11` *Type 2 diabetes mellitus*. Querying by a parent concept should include all of its descendants.

## Structures
* **Adjacency** (`icd10_hier`): each code with its immediate parent. Rolling up requires a recursive query.
* **Transitive closure** (`icd10_closure`, `rxnorm_closure`): every `(ancestor_code, descendant_code)` pair at all depths (depth 0 = self). Membership becomes a **single equality join** with no recursive CTE, which is fast, portable, and easy for Genie to generate.

## Examples
* **Diagnoses:** E10/E11/E13 → every specific diabetes code (**Diabetes Cohort**).
* **Medications:** statin ingredients → their clinical-drug codes (**SPD**).

## Business use
This is meaning via hierarchy, not flat code lists: specific codes are included automatically, without anyone maintaining them.

---

## E11.22 rolls up to two top-level conditions

E11.22 (*Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease*) has two parents, so it rolls up to two separate top-level conditions: **E11 Type 2 diabetes mellitus** and **N18 Chronic kidney disease (CKD)**. [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/29edada3c57e49f3a4b3b9b1d6850e50?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_b5ebb8)

| Top-level condition | Path | Steps up |
|---|---|---|
| **E11** Type 2 diabetes mellitus | E11.22 → **E11.2** (Type 2 diabetes with kidney complications) → E11 | 2 |
| **N18** Chronic kidney disease (CKD) | E11.22 → N18 (no code in between) | 1 |

[Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/29edada3c57e49f3a4b3b9b1d6850e50?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_b5ebb8) [Query Result](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/29edada3c57e49f3a4b3b9b1d6850e50?o=3464092709171785#embed-query_b368d1)

### Why this matters
- **E11.22 is counted in both groups.** It appears in a Type 2 diabetes cohort and in a CKD cohort. If you add up patient or encounter counts across the two, you'll count it twice.
- **How the paths were found.** The ancestor list (the ICD-10 closure table) shows every parent code and how many steps away it is, but it doesn't record the route between them. That table records E11.22 under both E11.2 and N18. [Code Subsumption (Closure Table)](https://fe-vm-vdm-classic-q6xfh3.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/79503778-0e4b-4f80-af63-47bbca97d35e?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=3464092709171785)
- **Limited scope.** The hierarchy table is a curated demo subset focused on diabetes, so it may not include every ICD-10 grouping above these codes. WITH RECURSIVE paths AS (
  SELECT `code`, `parent_code`, `name`, CAST(CONCAT(`code`, ' → ', COALESCE(`parent_code`,'(root)')) AS STRING) AS path, 1 AS lvl
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_hier` WHERE `code` = 'E11.22'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT h.`code`, h.`parent_code`, h.`name`, CONCAT(p.path, ' → ', COALESCE(h.`parent_code`,'(root)')), p.lvl + 1
  FROM paths p JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_hier` h ON h.`code` = p.`parent_code`
  WHERE p.lvl < 10
)
SELECT p.`code` AS top_code, p.`name` AS top_name, p.path
FROM paths p
WHERE p.`parent_code` IS NULL OR p.`parent_code` = '' OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`icd10_hier` h2 WHERE h2.`code` = p.`parent_code`)
